fixed.q:
Match the AI Ethics with its correct description.
Column I: I. Data privacy; II. K-anonymity; III. L-diversity

Column II: 1. It is a standard metric that measures how many users in a database share a particular attribute; 2. It is a trade-off between the amount of data collected and the performance of a product or service; 3. It extends the idea by merging several sensitive attributes together.
fixed.w: Data privacy is the trade-off between data collected and product performance (2); k-anonymity measures how many records share an attribute (1); l-diversity extends k-anonymity across sensitive attributes (3).

fixed.q: What is the advantage of exploratory Data Analysis in Big Data and Analytics?
o: Usually does not provide definitive answers
fixed.w: Exploratory data analysis is open-ended: it gives flexible ways to generate hypotheses rather than confirm them.

fixed.q: In AI biases many AI models are ______. I. deepfakes II. Black boxes III. K-anonymity
fixed.w: Many AI models are 'black boxes' because their internal decision process is not explainable.

fixed.q:
Match the categories of AI with its correct description.
Column I: I. Artificial Narrow Intelligence; II. Artificial General Intelligence; III. Super Intelligence

Column II: 1. Level of general and strong AI that is smarter than humans if that's possible; 2. Such system seems to act intelligently but they don't have any awareness of what they are doing; 3. Acting like a smart human and thinking like one with a conscious.
fixed.w: Narrow AI acts intelligently without awareness (2); general AI acts and thinks like a smart human (3); super-intelligence is smarter than humans (1).

fixed.q: From the challenges given below, which of the challenge does IoT adoption include?
fixed.w: Security and privacy of connected devices is a major challenge in IoT adoption.

fixed.q: The construction of computer-generated simulations that simulate real-world activities using interactive graphics software and hardware is called:
fixed.w: Virtual reality systems create interactive computer-generated simulations of the real world.

fixed.q: Haptic technology is used to provide ______ feedback to a user.
fixed.w: Haptic technology gives tactile (touch) feedback, e.g. phone vibration.

fixed.q: An individual's shared experience results in ______.
o: tacit knowledge, systematic knowledge and shared knowledge
fixed.w: Tacit knowledge: knowledge gained from personal experience is tacit.

fixed.q: Which qualitative statistic is difficult to quantify precisely?
fixed.w: 'value' is the qualitative factor that is hardest to quantify precisely.

fixed.q: In a management information system, what is/are the formal social unit(s) devoted to attaining specified goals?
fixed.w: An organisation is a formal social unit devoted to attaining specified goals.

fixed.q: A particular organisation or industry's most successful solutions or problem-solving methods are called ______.
fixed.w: An organisation's most successful solutions and methods are called 'best practices'. The official key says 'knowledge management'. (The official key was wrong here; this is the corrected answer.)

fixed.q: Which of the following refers to focusing on determining, organising, directing, facilitating and monitoring knowledge- related practices and activities required to achieve the desired business strategies and objectives with reference to knowledge management in organisations?
fixed.w: The management point of view of KM is about determining, organising, directing, facilitating and monitoring knowledge practices to meet business goals.

fixed.q: Which of the following refers to expertise and skills acquired by a person through experience or education, the theoretical or practical understanding of a subject?
fixed.w: Knowledge is expertise and skills gained through experience or education.

fixed.q: Which step of the knowledge management process involves adding value by discovering relationships, abstracting and sharing?
fixed.w: Knowledge refining adds value by discovering relationships, abstracting and preparing knowledge for sharing.

fixed.q: Interpretability, Format, Coherence and Compatibility refer to which quality of information with reference to Management Information System?
fixed.w: Interpretability, format, coherence and compatibility are representational qualities of information.

fixed.q: With reference to Management Information System, which of the following categories refers to information that is concerned with long-term policy decisions that define the objectives of a business and check how well these objectives are met?
fixed.w: Strategic information supports long-term policy decisions and objectives.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of Management Information System?
fixed.w: MIS components are people, hardware, software, data and procedures; 'education procedures' is not one.

fixed.q: Which of the following refers to a planned system of collecting, storing and disseminating data in the form of information needed to carry out the functions of management?
fixed.w: An MIS is a planned system for collecting, storing and disseminating information for management.

fixed.q: The lowest cost solution to developing a KM system is:
fixed.w: Building in-house is treated as the lowest-cost route to a KM system, since it reuses existing staff and infrastructure.

fixed.q: ______ is a set of interrelated components that collect (or retrieve), process, store and distribute information to support decision-making and control in an organisation.
o: Mini model of a processed system
Max model of a processed system
fixed.w: An information system is the set of interrelated components that collects, processes, stores and distributes information for decision-making and control.

fixed.q: DSS is a computer program application used to improve a company's ______ capabilities.
fixed.w: A DSS improves decision-making capabilities.

fixed.q: The set of processes developed in an organisation to create, gather, store, transfer and apply knowledge best describes:
fixed.w: Knowledge management is the set of processes to create, gather, store, transfer and apply knowledge.

fixed.q: Which of the following systems comprises word processing, electronic filing, electronic mail, message switching, data storage and data and voice communication?
fixed.w: Office Automation Systems include word processing, e-mail, e-filing and messaging.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT the purpose of a knowledge management system?
fixed.w: KM systems drive strategy, integrate and share knowledge; 'portability' is not a KM purpose.

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are key knowledge management process(es)? i) Knowledge gathering ii) Knowledge storage and organisation iii) Knowledge distribution iv) Knowledge use
fixed.w: Gathering, storage and organisation, distribution and use are all KM processes.

fixed.q: The main purpose of a/an ______ is to record, process, validate and store transactions that take place in various functional areas of a business for future retrieval and use.
fixed.w: A Transaction Processing System records, processes, validates and stores business transactions.

fixed.q: Which of the following are management information system resources? i) Hardware ii) Software iii) People iv) Data
fixed.w: MIS resources are hardware, software, people and data.

fixed.q:
Match the column Types of knowledge with the column Descriptions.
Types: a) Tacit knowledge; b) Implicit knowledge; c) Explicit knowledge

Descriptions: i) Captured within various document types such as manuals, reports and guides, allowing organisations to easily share knowledge across teams; ii) Typically acquired through experience and intuitively understood; iii) Also referred to as 'know-how' knowledge.
fixed.w: Tacit = experience-based and intuitive (ii), implicit = know-how (iii), explicit = documented (i).

fixed.q: ______ is known as the acquisition, storage, organization, retrieval, display and dissemination of information.
fixed.w: Information processing is the acquisition, storage, organisation, retrieval, display and dissemination of information.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a component of Decision Support System (DSS)? I. User interface II. Knowledge engine
fixed.w: A DSS has a database, a model base and a user interface (dialogue); as per the official key, a knowledge engine is also counted. Both.

fixed.q: Which of the following is not a key attribute of information?
fixed.w: Useful information is timely, accurate and relevant; 'isolation' is not one of its attributes.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a type of information system?
fixed.w: A Transaction Processing System (TPS) is a type of information system.

fixed.q: Which of the following characteristic(s) of expert systems is/are correct? I. The direction of interaction is from machine to the user. II. Its domain of knowledge is narrow. III. Information is produced by analysis of operational and external data.
fixed.w: In expert systems the machine questions the user (machine-to-user interaction) and the domain is narrow. Statement III describes an MIS.

fixed.q: Which of the following methods can be used to organise notes for interpreting an information? I. Flow chart II. Transition devices
fixed.w: Only I: flow charts organise notes for interpreting information, while transition devices are linking words rather than an organising method.

fixed.q: ______ is the process of identifying, organizing, storing and disseminating information within an organization.
fixed.w: Knowledge management identifies, organises, stores and disseminates knowledge within an organisation.

fixed.q: A fixed sum that is paid by customers for a service, typically on a monthly, quarterly or annual basis, is called ______ in electronic commerce.
fixed.w: A fixed periodic fee for a service is the subscription model.

fixed.q: The ______ E-commerce segment(s) is/are represented by OLX.
fixed.w: OLX is a consumer-to-consumer (C2C) marketplace.

fixed.q: Activities like packing goods, loading goods and shipping goods belong to which step of the e-commerce primary process?
fixed.w: Packing, loading and shipping goods are part of delivery/fulfilment.

fixed.q: With reference to stakeholders of e-commerce, business organisations abbreviated by 'B' may include
fixed.w: In e-commerce, 'B' (business) includes producers, manufacturers and sellers.

fixed.q: Who is the father of e-commerce in India?
fixed.w: K. Vaitheeswaran, co-founder of Indiaplaza, who is called the father of Indian e-commerce.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a barrier to e-commerce relevant to micro-environmental issues (external to the organisation)?
fixed.w: Internet infrastructure is the external (micro-environment) barrier to e-commerce.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a key driver of e-business?
fixed.w: A 'supplementary workforce' is not a key driver of e-business.

fixed.q: Which of the following business models falls into the category of 'Transplanted Real-World Business Models'?
fixed.w: The free-trial model is a 'transplanted' real-world model; digital products, access provision and freeware are native Internet models.

fixed.q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the strategies required to increase the visibility of e-commerce website? I. The website name should be sensible that it can be guessed. II. Uploading contents like special offers or eye catching information for the regular followers can increase traffic on the website. III. Icons of social networks on the website have no major influence on e-visibility.
fixed.w: A sensible, guessable name and attractive offers boost traffic, but social-media icons do help visibility, so III is false.

fixed.q: Which of the following business models fall into the category of 'Native Internet Business Models'? I. Library Model II. Subscription Model
fixed.w: The library model is a native Internet model; subscription is a transplanted (pre-Internet) model. So only I.

fixed.q: In cyber security, what remedy does the law provide?
fixed.w: Cyber laws (e.g. the IT Act) prescribe penalties such as imprisonment and fines as remedies.

fixed.q: Which among the following given below is correct in context of privacy issues in social media and online platforms?
o: The sharing on social media especially by children must be monitored at all times.
The addiction of social media does not hamper the academic performance of a student.
Rumours and fake news cannot put the administration at risk.
Mishandling of social media cannot create tension in the law and order.
fixed.w: Children's social-media sharing should be monitored; the other statements are false.

fixed.q: In context of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, which of the given following is correct?
o: "Child" means an individual who has not completed the age of eighteen years
"Digital personal data" means personal data in physical form
"Chairperson" does not mean the chairperson of the board
fixed.w: Under the DPDP Act 2023, a 'child' is an individual who has not completed eighteen years.

fixed.q: ______ enables the creator owner to earn recognition or financial benefit by using their creation or invention.
fixed.w: An intellectual property right lets the creator or owner earn recognition and financial benefit from the creation.

fixed.q: Over half of the e-waste generated in the developed world are exported to developing countries, mainly to ______, where metals like copper, iron, silicon, nickel and gold are recovered during recycling process.
fixed.w: India. Large volumes of e-waste from developed countries are shipped to India (and China, Ghana and others) for informal recycling.

fixed.q: Irreparable computer and other electronic goods are known as ______ in tech world.
fixed.w: Discarded or irreparable electronic goods are called electronic waste (e-waste).

fixed.q: The E-waste (management) rules 2016 of India, recognizes two broad categories: IT and telecommunication equipment and consumer electrical and electronics including which of the following material? I. Fluorescent II. Mercury
fixed.w: The E-Waste (Management) Rules 2016 also cover compact fluorescent and other mercury-containing lamps. Both are included.

fixed.q: In digital realm, which refers to the legal rights to protect invention or creation in intellectual property, are given to whom?
fixed.w: IP rights are granted to the creator or inventor.

fixed.q: IPR (Intellectual Property Right) is given for how much time, in digital realm?
o: Depending on case to case basis
fixed.w: IP rights are granted for a certain, limited period of time, e.g. a patent for 20 years.

fixed.q: In E-waste management, from which factors, there comes the exposure variability in electronic waste?
o: Quantity of the Pollutants in air
Management processes of the air pollution
fixed.w: Exposure variability depends mainly on the type of e-waste and the way it is processed.

fixed.q: Selling directly from a business to individual customers online (like Amazon retail) is:
fixed.w: B2C: business to consumer. B2B: between businesses. C2C: consumer to consumer (OLX). C2B: consumer to business (freelancers, Upwork).

fixed.q: A government buying from businesses through an online portal (like GeM) is:
fixed.w: B2G: business to government. GeM (Government e-Marketplace) is used for public procurement.

fixed.q: The structured computer-to-computer exchange of business documents between organisations is:
fixed.w: Electronic Data Interchange replaces paper documents such as purchase orders and invoices with standard electronic formats.

fixed.q: Software that integrates all business functions (finance, HR, production, sales) in one database is:
fixed.w: Enterprise Resource Planning integrates processes across departments. CRM handles customers; SCM handles the supply chain.

fixed.q: A system that supports senior managers with summarised, graphical strategic information is an:
fixed.w: ESS/EIS serve top management (strategic level). MIS serve middle managers. TPS serve the operational level.

fixed.q: In India, the main law dealing with cybercrime and electronic records is the:
fixed.w: The IT Act 2000 (amended 2008) gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures and defines cyber offences.

fixed.q: Section 66A of the IT Act was struck down by the Supreme Court in:
o: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
fixed.w: Shreya Singhal (2015) struck down 66A (offensive online messages) as unconstitutional. Puttaswamy (2017) declared privacy a fundamental right.

fixed.q: Under the IT Act, identity theft (fraudulent use of someone's password or digital signature) is punishable under:
fixed.w: 66C identity theft, 66D cheating by personation, 66E violation of privacy, 66F cyber terrorism, 67 obscene material.

fixed.q: Cyber terrorism is defined under which section of the IT Act?
fixed.w: Section 66F, punishable with imprisonment that may extend to life.

fixed.q: A patent in India is generally granted for:
fixed.w: Patents last 20 years from the filing date. Copyright lasts the author's lifetime + 60 years; a trademark lasts 10 years and is renewable.

fixed.q: Cloud model in which the provider supplies a ready-to-use application over the internet (e.g. Gmail) is:
fixed.w: SaaS: software. PaaS: development platform. IaaS: virtual machines, storage and networks (e.g. AWS EC2).

fixed.q: The "3 Vs" of Big Data are:
fixed.w: Doug Laney's 3 Vs: Volume (size), Velocity (speed), Variety (types). Veracity and Value are often added.

fixed.q: A distributed, tamper-resistant ledger of linked blocks is:
fixed.w: Each block holds the hash of the previous block, so altering one block breaks the chain.

fixed.q: The "new economy" refers to an economy driven mainly by:
fixed.w: The new (knowledge/digital) economy grew with the Internet; value comes from information and intangible assets.

fixed.q: Metcalfe's law says the value of a network grows roughly in proportion to:
o: The square of the number of users
fixed.w: Network effects: value ∝ n², which explains winner-take-most digital platforms.

fixed.q: The term "knowledge worker" was coined by:
fixed.w: Drucker (1959) described workers whose main capital is knowledge.

fixed.q: Intellectual capital of a firm includes:
fixed.w: Intellectual capital is intangible: employee know-how, processes/IP, and customer relationships.

fixed.q: Converting tacit knowledge into explicit knowledge (e.g. writing a manual from experience) is called:
fixed.w: Nonaka's SECI model: socialisation (tacit→tacit), externalisation (tacit→explicit), combination (explicit→explicit), internalisation (explicit→tacit).

theory.MIS, information systems & KM:
• Information system = hardware, software, data, people, procedures; collects, processes, stores and distributes information.
• Levels: TPS (operational, records transactions), MIS (middle management, routine reports), DSS (semi-structured decisions; database + model base + user interface), ESS/EIS (top management, strategic). OAS: word processing, e-mail, e-filing. Expert systems: knowledge base + inference engine.
• ERP integrates all functions; CRM manages customers; SCM manages the supply chain.
• Information quality: intrinsic, contextual, representational (interpretability, format, coherence), accessibility.
• Knowledge: tacit (in people, from experience) vs explicit (documented). KM process: create/gather, store, refine, share/transfer, apply. Best practices = most successful solutions.
theory.E-commerce:
• Models: B2B, B2C, C2C (OLX, eBay), C2B, B2G (GeM), G2C.
• Revenue models: subscription, advertising, transaction fee, sales, affiliate, freemium.
• EDI: computer-to-computer business documents. Payment gateway, EFT, digital wallets, UPI.
• Native internet models (library, freeware, information barter, digital products, access provider, search engine) vs transplanted real-world models (mail order, advertising, auction, subscription, direct marketing, free trial).
• Primary activities: order, payment, delivery/fulfilment, after-sales service.
theory.AI ethics, Big Data & IoT:
• AI types: Narrow (ANI), General (AGI), Super (ASI). Many AI models are black boxes; issues of bias, explainability and privacy. K-anonymity and l-diversity protect data privacy.
• Big Data 3 Vs: volume, velocity, variety (+ veracity, value). Tools: Hadoop (HDFS, MapReduce), Spark. Exploratory data analysis generates hypotheses.
• IoT: connected sensors/devices; main challenge is security.
• Cloud: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS; public, private, hybrid, community.
• VR (computer-simulated environments), AR (overlay on real world), haptics (tactile feedback), blockchain (hash-linked blocks).
theory.Cyber law, IPR, privacy & e-waste:
• IT Act 2000 (amended 2008): legal recognition of e-records and digital signatures. Sec 43 (damage to computer), 65 (tampering source code), 66 (hacking), 66A (struck down, Shreya Singhal 2015), 66B (stolen device), 66C (identity theft), 66D (cheating by personation), 66E (privacy), 66F (cyber terrorism, up to life), 67 (obscene material).
• DPDP Act 2023: "child" = under 18; consent-based processing; Data Protection Board.
• Puttaswamy (2017): privacy is a fundamental right.
• IPR: patent 20 years, copyright life + 60 years, trademark 10 years (renewable). IPR rewards the creator for a certain period.
• E-waste (Management) Rules 2016: EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility); categories include IT & telecom equipment and consumer electrical & electronics.
theory.Knowledge management & new economy:
• New (knowledge/digital) economy: value from information, knowledge, networks and intangibles; globalisation; e-business.
• Metcalfe's law: network value ∝ n². Network effects and low marginal cost of digital goods.
• Knowledge worker (Drucker). Intellectual capital = human + structural + relational capital.
• Nonaka's SECI: socialisation, externalisation, combination, internalisation. Tacit vs explicit knowledge.
• KM process: create/acquire, store, refine, share, apply; best practices; communities of practice.
